answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a time-locked work bond before it can transact: the bond is earned only by completing verified, useful work over weeks, so one operator spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay that cost thousands of times. Like water carving a canyon, the cost accumulates slowly and cannot be rushed; a gale of cheap new accounts hits a glacier of sunk, verifiable effort. An attacker who burns one identity loses its bond and history, so faking a crowd costs more than the fraud it enables.
